podcast.title: Band Origins and Genre (1989-2000)
podcast.body: Hailing from Ottawa, Furnace Face was an indie band primarily rooted in punk rock, with a distinctive inclination for satirizing metal music. They were active for approximately 10 years, from 1989 to around 2000. "I got a bunch of email from people asking about Furnace Face, the indie band from Ottawa. They were mostly punk, but also had a thing about making fun of metal. They had something going for about 10 years, 1989 to around 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lineup Expansion and On-Stage Pyro Incident (1997)
podcast.body: The band continued to perform gigs into the 2000s, expanding to a four-piece lineup. A notable incident occurred in 1997 when bass player Slow Tom was involved in an on-stage pyro accident, from which he fortunately recovered. "They were gigs into the 2000s when they expanded to a four piece. [...] There was a scary moment in 1997 when bass player Slow Tom ended up at the wrong end of some on-stage pyro, but he recovered."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Indie Success, Mainstream Limitation
podcast.body: Although the band never managed to break into the mainstream alt-rock scene, they achieved a respectable level of success within the indie music world, including winning some awards. "And although they never really broke into the mainstream alt-roxy, they did, you know, okay. [...] They won some awards in the indie world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Recovery from On-Stage Pyro Incident (1997)
xref.body: In 1997, as the bass player for Furnace Face, Slow Tom was involved in an on-stage pyro incident. Despite the scary moment, he fully recovered from the experience. "There was a scary moment in 1997 when bass player Slow Tom ended up at the wrong end of some on-stage pyro, but he recovered."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Current Country Band and Freelance Composer
xref.body: Currently, Slow Tom fronts a country band that performs occasionally, and this group also features Furnace Face drummer Dave Dudley. He additionally works as a freelance composer, creating music for film and television projects. "These days, Tom has a country band that plays the occasional gig, and that group also features Furnace Face drummer Dave Dudley. Tom also has at least three solo albums to his credit, and he's a freelance composer for film and TV these days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
